concept.body: Solving a right triangle completely = all sides + all angles. Inventory what you have. Angle + side: use sin/cos/tan for the other sides, 90° minus the known acute angle for the other angle. Two sides: Pythagoras for the third, one inverse-trig call for an angle, complement for the last. Cross-check with a² + b² = c².

explanationVariants: The hypotenuse is known, so SUBTRACT squares: √144 = 12.

widget.prompt: Hypotenuse 13, one leg 5. The other leg = ?

commonErrors.feedback: 13.93 ≈ √(169 + 25) ADDS — but 13 is the hypotenuse, so its square is the total. Subtract: √144 = 12.
8 = 13 − 5 subtracts plain lengths. Pythagoras subtracts SQUARES: √(169 − 25) = 12.

steps.body: “Solve the right triangle” means find EVERYTHING: all three sides, all three angles. You never need six separate hunts — the right angle is free, the acute angles sum to 90°, and Pythagoras links the sides. Given one acute angle and one side, or any two sides, the rest cascades.

widget.prompt: One acute angle is 37°. Drag to it, read adj/hyp, and note what the other acute angle must be.
widget.successFeedback: The other acute angle is 53°, because the two must total 90°. Solving a right triangle completely means one angle plus one side is enough — the third angle comes free, and the ratios supply the rest.
widget.scaleFeedback: Resize the triangle a couple of times; the ratio at 37° must not depend on how big it is.

steps.body: Case one: **an angle and a side.** From θ = 37° and hypotenuse 10, sine and cosine deliver both legs — opposite = 10·sin 37° ≈ 6.02, adjacent = 10·cos 37° ≈ 7.99. Then audit: 6.02² + 7.99² ≈ 100 ✓. The Pythagorean check catches ratio mix-ups before they cost you.

widget.prompt: θ = 37°, hypotenuse 10. Find the leg OPPOSITE θ (2 decimals).

commonErrors.feedback: 7.99 = 10·cos 37° is the ADJACENT leg. Opposite comes from sine: 10·sin 37° ≈ 6.02.
7.54 = 10·tan 37° — but 10 is the HYPOTENUSE, and tangent never uses it. 10·sin 37° ≈ 6.02.

steps.body: Case two: **two sides, no angle.** Pythagoras finds the third side; inverse trig finds an angle; the complement finishes. Legs 9 and 12: hypotenuse = √(81+144) = √225 = 15. Angle opposite the 9: tan⁻¹(9/12) ≈ 36.87°. Other angle: 90 − 36.87 = 53.13°. Done — three tools, one pass.

explanationVariants: Legs 9 and 12 are 3·4 and 4·3... i.e. the 3-4-5 triple scaled by 3, so the hypotenuse is 15.

commonErrors.feedback: 7.94 ≈ √(144 − 81) subtracts, which finds a LEG when the hypotenuse is known. Both givens are legs: add → 15.
225 is the hypotenuse SQUARED. Take the square root: 15.

explanationVariants: Opposite 9, adjacent 12 — tangent's pair — so tan⁻¹(0.75) ≈ 36.87°.

widget.prompt: Same triangle (legs 9 and 12, hypotenuse 15): find the angle OPPOSITE the leg of length 9, in degrees (2 decimals).

commonErrors.feedback: 53.13° = tan⁻¹(12/9) faces the 12. Your angle faces the 9: tan⁻¹(9/12) ≈ 36.87°.
48.59° = sin⁻¹(9/12) puts a LEG (12) in the hypotenuse's seat. Either tan⁻¹(9/12) or sin⁻¹(9/15): ≈ 36.87°.

widget.prompt: Besides the right angle, what is the MINIMUM extra information that determines a right triangle completely?

options.label: Any two sides, or one side plus one acute angle
options.feedback: Either package pins the triangle: Pythagoras + inverse trig handle two sides; trig ratios + the complement handle side-and-angle.

options.label: Both acute angles
options.feedback: Two angles fix only the SHAPE — every similar copy shares them. Without a side, the size floats free.

options.label: All three sides are always required
options.feedback: Three sides is more than needed: from any two, Pythagoras rebuilds the third.

options.label: One acute angle alone
options.feedback: One angle gives shape but no size — same problem as knowing both angles. A side must anchor the scale.

hints: The 40 touches the 25° angle: it's the ADJACENT leg, and you want the hypotenuse.
cos 25° = 40/hyp — the unknown sits on the bottom.
explanationVariants: cos 25° = 40/hyp → hyp = 40 ÷ cos 25° ≈ 44.14 — longer than 40, as a hypotenuse must be.
Adjacent known, hypotenuse wanted: divide the adjacent by cos 25° ≈ 0.9063 to get ≈ 44.14.

widget.prompt: θ = 25°; the leg ADJACENT to θ is 40. Find the hypotenuse (2 decimals).

commonErrors.feedback: 36.25 = 40·cos 25° multiplies — yielding a hypotenuse SHORTER than a leg, impossible. Divide: 40 ÷ cos 25° ≈ 44.14.
94.65 = 40 ÷ sin 25° uses sine — but 40 is ADJACENT, cosine's side. 40 ÷ cos 25° ≈ 44.14.
18.65 = 40·tan 25° is the OPPOSITE leg — a real side, but not the one asked. Hypotenuse: ≈ 44.14.

takeaways: Angle + side: trig ratios give the missing sides; 90°-complement gives the angle.
Two sides: Pythagoras → third side; inverse trig → an angle; complement → the last.
Always audit with a² + b² = c² and the longest-side rule.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: point these tools at the world — angles of elevation and depression.
